options.parentAdvice: Remind your child of when a short vowel sound is used compared to the long vowel sound. Write the word "cat" on a piece of paper. Have your child identify if each letter is a consonant or vowel. Once your child confirms have them write a "c" or a "v" under each letter in cat. Ask your child to point to the vowel, then ask them does a vowel or consonant come after the vowel in the word. Once they respond with a consonant, remind them that if there is a consonant after a vowel in a one syllable word then the vowel will say its short sound. Have the child read the word. Practice with: Band, fan, swam

Create a 3 by 3 chart and write the word could in several boxes along with decodable words such as cob and cod. You and your child will go back and forth reading a word and marking either an X or O over it. Hint: leave the word 'could' for your child to mark.

Remind your child of when a short vowel sound is used compared to the long vowel sound. Write the word "top" on a piece of paper. Have your child identify if each letter is a consonant or vowel. Once your child confirms have them write a "c" or a "v" under each letter in top. Ask your child to point to the vowel, then ask them does a vowel or consonant come after the vowel in the word. Once they respond with a consonant, remind them that if there is a consonant after a vowel in a one syllable word then the vowel will say its short sound. Have the child read the word. Practice with: Pod, block, blob
